in_english.name: Rachele
in_english.meaning: Ewe, female sheep, loved by God
in_english.long_meaning: Rachele is the Italian variant of Rachel, originating from the Hebrew name 'רחל' (Rachel) meaning 'ewe, female sheep'. In the Bible, Rachel was the beloved wife of Jacob (Genesis 29-31). The name symbolizes divine love, loyalty, and spiritual devotion. Throughout Christian tradition, Rachele represents feminine virtues and maternal love.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rachele, derived from the Biblical name Rebecca, is of Hebrew origin. Rebecca is one of the most significant women in the Hebrew Bible, known for her unwavering faith and strong character. Her name has been passed down through generations and has become a popular given name among Christians, particularly in Italy, where it is commonly used. Rachele carries the cultural weight of Rebecca's legacy, representing strength, resilience, and faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rachele has deep spiritual significance, as it means 'woman of God'. This name reminds us of the power and strength that comes from trusting in God and relying on His divine help. In the Hebrew tradition, the name Rebecca symbolizes the covenant between God and his people, bringing to mind the promise of God's help and support in times of need. Rachele's name is a constant reminder to stay strong in faith and to seek God's guidance in all aspects of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rachele, derived from Rachel in the Old Testament, represents profound compassion and emotional depth. It symbolizes the ability to bear children of promise amidst trials and the deep, unending love of a mother.
